prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In Frames 1 and 2, the depth map captures a lounge corner receding from the bright near end of a dark couch on the right (~0.8–1 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and the rug below, past a snare drum (~2 m) and a grey armchair (~2.5–3 m, about 0.5–1 m left of the drum and couch, facing toward the foreground), to a lamp (~3.5 m) and back wall (~4.5–5 m). Across Frames 3 to 5, as the camera wearer turns roughly 90 degrees left toward a larger windowed room, a bright foreground mass (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach) briefly enters the lower-right in Frame 3 occluding the rug and armchair, followed by a person appearing on the far left edge in Frame 4 (~0.6–0.8 m) who moves further into the left foreground in Frame 5 (~0.5–0.7 m, within arm's reach and cut off at the left and bottom edges). In Frames 4 and 5, this close person stands ~4 m in front of two white midground couches (~4.5 m and ~5.5 m away, ~1 m apart around a coffee table) and ~5.5 m left-front of a far-right chair (~6 m), facing right and slightly toward the camera wearer while occluding the leftmost white couch in Frame 5. The depth map clearly reveals the 3D surface gradient of the dark tufted couch in Frames 1–2 and isolates the heavily backlit, nearly black silhouette of the close person in Frames 4–5 from the dark interior, which is hard to see in RGB alone; however, it is unreliable on the transparent glass coffee table in the lower-left of Frames 1–2 (which nearly disappears into the floor) and saturates to flat white on the close person in Frame 5, obscuring facial orientation and torso contours.
descriptions.segmentation: In Frames 1 and 2, the instance segmentation map outlines the large foreground couch on the right (~0.8–2.5 m, with its near corner within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and the armchair to its left (~2.5–3 m, ~1 m from the couch, facing forward and right), while leaving the surrounding floor, snare drum, and background unmasked. As the camera turns left through Frame 3 into a wide room in Frames 4 and 5, masks identify a close person on the left edge (~0.5–0.8 m, within arm's reach and partly out of view at the left/bottom borders), two white couches in the midground (~4.5 m and ~5.5 m away, ~1 m apart facing toward each other), and a small chair on the far right (~6 m away, ~3 m right of the center couch). Between Frames 4 and 5, the foreground person shifts rightward into the left half of the view—facing right and looking roughly toward the camera wearer—and occludes the left white couch and coffee table behind them. The segmentation map makes it easy to separate the dark, backlit foreground person in Frames 4–5 from the shadowed wall and pinpoints the distant far-right chair (~6 m) amidst background clutter, which are hard to discern in RGB; however, it is unreliable when it mislabels the armchair as 'couch' and overlaps 'bed'/'couch' labels in Frame 2, misses the snare drum and glass table entirely, fails completely during Frame 3's motion blur, and drops the unoccluded center white couch in Frame 5.
descriptions.pose: Across the five-frame sequence as the camera wearer turns left from a lounge corner (Frames 1–2) past a close lower-right occluder (Frame 3, ~0.3–0.5 m) toward a wide studio room with midground couches (~4.5–5.5 m) and a close person standing on the left (Frames 4–5, ~0.5–0.8 m), the pose map remains completely blank in Frames 1, 3, 4, and 5. Its only output is a single yellow body skeleton in Frame 2 positioned in the upper-left midground (~2.5–3 m from the camera wearer, ~1 m left of the snare drum and ~1.5 m from the right couch, outside arm's reach), showing a tilted torso and clustered upper-left head keypoints angled downward and to the right with no magenta hand keypoints. In contrast, the actual person who enters on the left within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.5–0.8 m) in Frame 4 and stands prominently in the left foreground in Frame 5—facing right and looking roughly toward the camera wearer with their lower body and left side cut off by the frame border while occluding the distant left couch (~5.5 m)—has no skeleton rendered at all. Consequently, the pose map provides no valid spatial detail beyond RGB and is completely unreliable here: it hallucinates a human pose onto the inanimate grey armchair and throw pillow in Frame 2, while failing to detect the real foreground person in Frames 3–5 due to heavy backlighting, silhouette underexposure, and partial truncation at the image edges.
